newsitem.title: USA: Majority of Americans say U.S. tax system unfair - poll.
newsitem.headline: Majority of Americans say U.S. tax system unfair - poll.

text.p: A majority of Americans believe the federal income tax system is unfair, and about half believe they are paying more than their share, according to a CBS News poll released on Saturday.
The poll, a nationwide random telephone survey of 1,347 adults, was conducted on April 2-5. It found that 55 percent of Americans believe the system is unfair and 44 percent think it is fair.

The poll showed that the higher the income bracket, the more likely people were to think they were paying too much in taxes. Sixty-eight percent of those with a total annual income of more than $75,000 said they were paying more than their fair shair in taxes, and 30 percent said they were paying about the right amount.
Among people with a total income of less than $15,000, 60 percent thought they were paying the right amount and 31 percent thought they were paying too much.
The figures for the total population showed that 49 percent believed they were over-paying and 47 percent believed they were paying about the right amount.

CBS said that for the past 20 years more than half the public has said the federal income tax system is unfair to people like themselves and that the latest poll results reflect "a longstanding sentiment about the tax system and have remained almost unchanged since 1977."

The poll also found that as of April 5, just 10 days from the filing deadline, 38 percent of American taxpayers said they had not filed their federal income tax returns. The worst procrastinators were those who were better off and those who had to file more complicated returns.
The poll had a margin of error of plus or minus 3 percentage points for results based on the entire sample.
